and likewise he was born on Atzeres,
as it says in the holy sefarim,
for HaKadosh Baruch Hu fills out
and for this reason on Atzeres we read
And it says in the Ra'aya Mehemna, Parshas Emor
which are the two letters hei;
for this is the bread of Torah,
ה׳ ה׳ מִן הַמּוֹצִיא לֶחֶם מִן הָאָרֶץ.
the two heis of 'HaMotzi lechem min ha'aretz.'"
That is: the letter hei of "ha'aretz"
is called in the holy Zohar "earth,"
is the upper hei, which is Binah,
which is the one who "brings forth," etc.
And both of them are the middah
who is a chariot for the middah of Malchus;
we call it Torah she'b'al peh" —
and this is the lower hei.
וַיֵּשֶׁב עַל כִּסֵּא ה׳ (דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים א כט, כג),
"And he sat upon the throne of Hashem" (Divrei HaYamim I 29:23),
הָיָה רַבָּן שֶׁל בַּעֲלֵי רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ,
was the master of those who possess ruach hakodesh,
that is, a spirit from the supernal Kodesh,
which is the aspect of Torah she'b'al peh,
And likewise Dovid HaMelech, alav hashalom,
is "the man who was raised on high" —
who raised up the yoke of teshuvah
and this is the upper hei, Binah
("and his heart will understand and he will return" — Yeshayah 6:10);
and it is written, "Then you will understand the fear of Hashem,
and find the knowledge of G-d" (Mishlei 2:5).
And in the first utterance it is written:
וְרוּחַ אֱלֹהִים מְרַחֶפֶת וְגוֹ׳ (בְּרֵאשִׁית א, ב);
"And the spirit of G-d hovered, etc." (Bereishis 1:2);
זֶה רוּחוֹ שֶׁל מֶלֶךְ הַמָּשִׁיחַ וְכוּלֵּי;
"This is the spirit of Melech HaMashiach, etc.";
"hovering over the face of the waters" —
which is likened to water, etc.
And this is Dovid HaMelech, alav hashalom,
as it is written: "And Dovid My servant
shall be a prince to them forever" (Yechezkel 37:25).
of the aspect of Torah she'b'al peh
will be in the future, through Mashiach;
כׇּל הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁאַתְּ לָמֵד בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
"All the Torah that you learn in this world
of the World to Come, etc."
And in truth, the two matters are one;
is from the dew of Atika,
And teshuvah, though it was always effective,
was only to be saved from punishment;
but that it turn willful sins into merits —
this they merited only at Matan Torah,
that is, that it becomes clear
that they are bound at the root to Hashem Yisbarach
at the very beginning of Thought.
on what Chazal say in Shabbos (89b):
אִם יִהְיוּ חֲטָאֵיכֶם כַּשָּׁנִים (יְשַׁעְיָה א, יח)
"'If your sins be like scarlet' (Yeshayah 1:18) — like these years
from the six days of Creation, etc.";
which is the deeds of the wicked,
as Chazal say in Bereishis Rabbah (2:5);
and Hashem Yisbarach created darkness first,
and there is no light except from within the darkness.
(of what Chazal say in Tanchuma, Haazinu 4:
"One who does teshuvah, He shows them favor;
and not to the nations, etc."; see there),
it was only to be saved from punishment;
but that it turn sins into merits —
only Yisrael merited this, at Matan Torah.
And this is what Chazal say
(in Rashi's commentary, from the Mechilta, Shemos 20:2):
"Because He revealed Himself at the Sea
as an elder full of compassion, etc."
which is the revelation of the middah of Atika.
וְאָז זָכוּ לְאוֹר תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
And then they merited the light of Torah she'b'al peh,
whose radiance is from the dew of Atika,
by which willful sins become as merits;
to which the two heis point:
the mouth, Torah she'b'al peh, etc.
